title: Adobe and Google Deepen Pact: Gemini Reaches Photoshop, Acrobat Comes to Gmail
excerpt: Announced at Adobe MAX on November 10, the expanded partnership puts PDF editing inside Gmail and Drive and Google's AI models inside Adobe's creative apps — though key pieces have no launch date yet.
body:
• Adobe and Google announced an expanded partnership on November 10 at Adobe MAX: Acrobat is coming to Google Drive and Gmail as a suggested app with an "Edit with" entry point in file previews.
  • Google's AI models will power more of Acrobat AI, including conversational PDF editing, while Adobe's Gemini Omni, Veo and Nano Banana models are already available inside Firefly, Photoshop, Premiere and Adobe Express, Adobe says.
  • Most of this is announced, not shipped: neither company gave a launch date or price for editing PDFs from Gmail, and a Google DeepMind model being customised for Photoshop is described as an exploration.
  • What it means for you: if your workday runs through Gmail and PDFs, the downloads-and-reuploads step is the part both companies say they are removing — but only once the integrations actually arrive.

Adobe and Google are tying their products much closer together. In an expanded strategic partnership announced November 10 at Adobe MAX, the companies said Acrobat will be available inside Google Workspace — through Google Drive and Gmail — as a suggested app, with an "Edit with" entry point in file previews. Google's AI models, in turn, will power more of Adobe's software, and Adobe's creative tools will surface inside Gemini, Gemini Enterprise and AI Mode in Google Search.

The PDF workflow is the centrepiece

For the hundreds of millions of people who receive PDFs by email, the practical change is the Gmail and Drive integration. Google put it plainly in its own announcement: users will "soon" have a direct pathway from a file preview into Acrobat, rather than downloading an attachment, editing it elsewhere and re-uploading it. Adobe will also add Google's AI models to the set powering Acrobat AI, which it says will support conversational PDF editing, faster document understanding, and quicker creation of presentations, resumes and reports. Adobe says more than 400 billion PDFs are opened with Acrobat each year, and that its creative and productivity tools serve more than 1 billion monthly active users.

Neither company announced a date or a price for the Workspace integration, and Google's wording — "soon" — is the only timeline on offer. Readers should treat this as a roadmap announcement, not a feature they can use today.

Gemini models inside Adobe's creative apps

The part that is already live, according to Adobe, is model choice inside its creative tools: customers can already use Google's Gemini Omni, Veo and Nano Banana models in Firefly, Photoshop, Premiere and Adobe Express for image and video generation and editing. Beyond that, Adobe and Google DeepMind will collaborate on AI editing, starting with Photoshop, exploring the customisation of a Google image model that could enable near-real-time edits, prompt-based adjustment and choosing among generated variants. Both companies describe that work as exploratory, and Gadgets 360 notes there is no word on when it might arrive.

"By further connecting our respective platforms, we are giving creators and enterprise teams a powerful, integrated environment to turn their ideas into high-impact content."

— Thomas Kurian, CEO, Google Cloud

The enterprise angle

For businesses, Adobe will expand its connectors in Gemini and Gemini Enterprise to cover Acrobat and additional creative tools, so employees can enhance images, customise designs and work with PDFs inside a chat. Adobe's CX Enterprise Coworker agent will also be usable in Gemini Enterprise, aimed at teams designing graphics, working with PDFs and launching marketing campaigns without switching apps. "Our expanded partnership combines Google's frontier AI with Adobe's industry-leading creative and productivity tools at global scale," said Anil Chakravarthy, Adobe's president and incoming CEO.

What to watch

Two things will decide whether this matters beyond the press releases: when the Drive and Gmail Acrobat pathway actually switches on, and whether the DeepMind collaboration produces a Photoshop model that feels different from the generative tools Adobe already ships. Until the first of those lands, the announcement is best read as both companies defending their home turf — Google's inbox, Adobe's document and creative stack — by making each other's products easier to reach.
